claims.title: Supplier paperwork may be intercepted en route to the vendor portal
claims.description: If the unverified `encryption_in_transit` on `flow:entity:supplier>process:supplier-portal>upload-documents` resolves to no effective transport encryption, an observer on the path from `entity:supplier` to `process:supplier-portal` can intercept insurance certificates, food-safety audits, and supplier staff contact details. This is a decided crossing from the public-internet zone, although the supplier endpoint placement was inferred; the model does not verify either protocol or transport protection. The captured PII and business-critical compliance material can be used to target suppliers and exposes documents before they reach `store:document-store`.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional: `flow:entity:supplier>process:supplier-portal>upload-documents` crosses into the vendor platform from `entity:supplier` in `boundary:public-internet`, while its protocol and `encryption_in_transit` are unstated. Impact is medium because the flow carries `pii` and business-critical compliance documents, whose disclosure is irreversible.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce protected supplier-to-portal transport
mitigations.detail: Establish the protocol and transport posture for `flow:entity:supplier>process:supplier-portal>upload-documents`; require TLS 1.2+ with modern configuration for the public portal connection and record the resulting `encryption_in_transit` value.

claims.title: Category-manager document reviews may be intercepted across the corporate-to-vendor boundary
claims.description: If `encryption_in_transit` on `flow:entity:category-manager>process:supplier-portal>review-documents` is not effectively protected, an attacker able to observe the corporate-network-to-vendor-platform path can intercept document-review activity, approvals, and rejections handled by `process:supplier-portal`. The channel is a decided trust-boundary crossing, but both protocol and category-manager authentication remain unverified. Disclosure of review information can reveal supplier compliance status and support targeted social engineering against `entity:category-manager` or suppliers whose documents are held in `store:document-store`.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce protected category-manager transport
mitigations.detail: Establish the protocol and `encryption_in_transit` state for `flow:entity:category-manager>process:supplier-portal>review-documents` and require TLS for every review request and response.

claims.title: Portal-to-document-store traffic may expose uploaded paperwork
claims.description: If the unverified `encryption_in_transit` on `flow:process:supplier-portal>store:document-store>store-documents` resolves to absent or ineffective protection, an observer with a foothold on the vendor-platform path can intercept uploaded compliance documents as `process:supplier-portal` writes them to `store:document-store`. The model also leaves the protocol and service-to-store authentication unverified. Captured PII and compliance documents can be correlated with the later review activity handled by the portal.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the attacker needs a foothold on the intra-`boundary:vendor-platform` path and `encryption_in_transit` is unverified. Impact is medium because `store:document-store` and the flow carry `pii` and business-critical compliance documents.

mitigations.summary: Require authenticated encryption on the portal storage hop
mitigations.detail: Verify the protocol and require TLS or an equivalent authenticated encrypted channel for `flow:process:supplier-portal>store:document-store>store-documents`, including certificate validation between the portal and its document storage service.

claims.title: Nightly supplier extract may be intercepted while the vendor sends it to the landing bucket
claims.description: If `encryption_in_transit` on `flow:entity:portal-vendor>store:landing-bucket>push-nightly-extract` is not effective, an observer on the vendor-platform-to-cloud-account path can intercept the nightly supplier data extract before it reaches `store:landing-bucket`. This is a decided boundary crossing, though the vendor endpoint zone was inferred. The source describes the file as arriving as a plain CSV, but does not settle whether the transport channel was protected; this draft is conditional on that unresolved transport fact. The captured extract can disclose the supplier records subsequently loaded by `process:supplier-master-service` into `store:supplier-database`.

quotes.text: The runbook for the landing bucket says the file arrives as a plain CSV and is picked up as-is.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `flow:entity:portal-vendor>store:landing-bucket>push-nightly-extract` crosses from the vendor platform into the cloud account and both protocol and transport encryption are unstated. Impact is medium because the extract carries `pii` and business-critical supplier data that is later persisted in `store:supplier-database`.

mitigations.summary: Use a verified encrypted vendor-to-bucket delivery channel
mitigations.detail: Require a documented TLS or mutually authenticated managed-transfer channel for `flow:entity:portal-vendor>store:landing-bucket>push-nightly-extract`, verify the receiving endpoint, and record the resolved transport control.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt the extract independently of transport
mitigations.detail: Have the vendor encrypt and sign each extract for a key controlled by the cloud-account recipient, so a captured delivery does not disclose the CSV contents.

claims.title: Supplier-master reads from the landing bucket may be visible on an unverified internal channel
claims.description: If `encryption_in_transit` on `flow:process:supplier-master-service>store:landing-bucket>load-extract` is absent or ineffective, an attacker with a foothold on the cloud-account path can intercept the nightly supplier extract while `process:supplier-master-service` reads it from `store:landing-bucket`. The protocol and authentication for this read flow are also unstated. The intercepted PII and business-critical records can be retained independently of the service and used to identify or target the suppliers subsequently represented in `store:supplier-database`.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the attacker needs a foothold on the intra-`boundary:cloud-account` read path and its `encryption_in_transit` value is unknown. Impact is medium because the landing-bucket extract is tagged `pii` and business-critical data.

mitigations.detail: Verify and enforce TLS for `flow:process:supplier-master-service>store:landing-bucket>load-extract`, including endpoint validation and a workload identity that can access only the required object prefix.

claims.title: Supplier records may be intercepted while the master service writes the database
claims.description: If `encryption_in_transit` on `flow:process:supplier-master-service>store:supplier-database>write-supplier-records` resolves to no effective protection, an attacker with a foothold on the cloud-account path can intercept supplier records as `process:supplier-master-service` writes them to `store:supplier-database`. Both the protocol and connection authentication are unverified. The attacker obtains PII and business-critical record content that remains useful for supplier targeting even after the nightly load completes.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because observation requires a foothold within `boundary:cloud-account` and `encryption_in_transit` on the write flow is unstated. Impact is medium because the flow writes `pii` and business-critical supplier records into `store:supplier-database`.

mitigations.detail: Establish and enforce TLS with certificate validation for `flow:process:supplier-master-service>store:supplier-database>write-supplier-records`, and record the service identity authorized to write records.

claims.title: Vendor document-store copies may expose supplier paperwork if encryption at rest is absent
claims.description: `store:document-store` holds PII and business-critical uploaded compliance documents, but its `encryption_at_rest` attribute is unknown. If this resolves to unencrypted storage, an attacker who obtains a storage-layer copy, such as operational media or an export associated with this store, can read the documents without using `process:supplier-portal` or its normal authentication path. The disclosure enables targeting suppliers and category managers using the document and contact information. This is conditional on the unresolved at-rest control and does not assert that the vendor store is unencrypted.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `store:document-store` has no verified `encryption_at_rest` control, so a storage copy may be readable if obtained. Impact is medium because the store holds `pii` and business-critical compliance documents, notwithstanding its unknown data classification.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce encryption for document-store data and copies
mitigations.detail: Obtain the vendor's verifiable at-rest encryption and key-management posture for `store:document-store`; require managed encryption covering operational copies and restrict export and storage-administration access.

claims.title: Landing-bucket copies may disclose the complete nightly supplier extract
claims.description: `store:landing-bucket` contains the nightly supplier extract and is tagged with PII and business-critical data, while `encryption_at_rest` is unknown. If storage encryption is absent or ineffective, a party obtaining a copy of the bucket's underlying data or an operational export can read the plain extract without authenticating through `process:supplier-master-service`. The extract is then loaded into `store:supplier-database`, so one copied file can expose the supplier dataset before its normal processing path. This is a conditional storage-copy threat, not an assertion that the bucket lacks encryption.

quotes.text: The runbook for the landing bucket says the file arrives as a plain CSV and is picked up as-is.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `store:landing-bucket` has unverified `encryption_at_rest` and a copied storage artifact bypasses the application path. Impact is medium because the bucket holds a supplier extract tagged `pii` and business-critical data.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt the landing bucket and all retained object versions
mitigations.detail: Establish the at-rest posture for `store:landing-bucket`; require managed-key encryption for objects, versions, and operational copies, and tightly limit object export and key-use permissions.
Encrypt the delivered extract before storage and have `process:supplier-master-service` decrypt it only in memory under a scoped workload identity.

claims.title: Supplier-database storage copies may disclose all loaded supplier records
claims.description: `store:supplier-database` holds supplier records tagged as PII and business-critical data, but its `encryption_at_rest` attribute is unknown. If that unknown resolves to no effective encryption, an attacker obtaining a storage-layer copy can read the loaded records directly rather than through `process:supplier-master-service` or an application query path. The disclosure creates a retained corpus of supplier information that can be used for targeted fraud or social engineering. This draft is conditional on the unresolved encryption-at-rest state.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `store:supplier-database` has no verified `encryption_at_rest` control and a storage copy bypasses its normal access path. Impact is medium because it holds the loaded supplier-record corpus tagged `pii` and business-critical data.

mitigations.summary: Enforce encryption at rest for the supplier database
mitigations.detail: Verify the `encryption_at_rest` state of `store:supplier-database`, require managed-key encryption for database storage and operational copies, and restrict backup, export, and decrypt permissions.

claims.title: Unverified landing-bucket read authentication may let an unauthorized party obtain the extract
claims.description: `process:supplier-master-service` reads the nightly supplier extract from `store:landing-bucket` through `flow:process:supplier-master-service>store:landing-bucket>load-extract`, but authentication on that read path is unknown. If the bucket does not require a narrowly scoped authenticated workload identity, an attacker able to reach its read interface can obtain the extract directly rather than compromising the supplier-master service. The resulting PII and business-critical data can then be retained or used to target suppliers, and the same records subsequently populate `store:supplier-database`. This is conditional on the unverified authentication control, not a claim that bucket access is unauthenticated.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because authentication on the established read flow into `store:landing-bucket` is unknown, so it must be evaluated as potentially absent, though the attacker must reach the cloud-account bucket interface. Impact is medium because the readable extract is tagged `pii` and business-critical data and feeds `store:supplier-database`.

mitigations.summary: Require least-privilege workload authentication for bucket reads
mitigations.detail: Set and verify authentication on `flow:process:supplier-master-service>store:landing-bucket>load-extract` using a dedicated workload identity limited to the required object prefix; deny anonymous, broad-account, and cross-environment reads.

mitigations.summary: Audit and alert on extract reads
mitigations.detail: Record object-read identity, source context, and object name for the landing bucket, and alert on reads outside the scheduled supplier-master workload.
